issue_request: FHIR-7058 was a Published FHIR-core AllergyIntolerance issue, resolved Not Persuasive with Modification, asking why sunlight and similar physical-agent reactions were excluded from AllergyIntolerance instead of following the C-CDA design. The approved resolution replaced the older misuse sentence with guidance that the allergy/intolerance list supports patient-safety decision support and that reactions triggered by light, heat, cold, pressure, vibration, and similar physical stimuli should be recorded as Conditions on the problem list, not as AllergyIntolerance.
initial_application: The resolution appears to have been applied by commit 3ea42ecce8fc3a87379eb817328e7bdabebf8a5a on 2015-08-21, which replaced the old physical-agent/sunlight misuse sentence in source/allergyintolerance/allergyintolerance-introduction.xml with the approved decision-support/problem-list wording. A later 2015 cleanup commit adjusted capitalization and nearby text without changing the substantive rule.
additional_context: AllergyIntolerance is active in the current build through source/fhir.ini, and the current introduction still includes the FHIR-7058 guidance in the Misuse section with a link to Condition. Related US Core/DAF issue FHIR-8140 was resolved no-change and its comments recognized that AllergyIntolerance had moved from explicit sunlight text to broader physical-stimuli wording. Searches of Zulip and Confluence found no directly relevant community record that conflicts with the Jira/source/history conclusion.
